text:
marco: heads-up — since 04:28 UTC we're seeing steady tiny-pod evictions in ap-southeast2. pending-small-pods: 240 -> 780, evictions +150%. Fragmentation heatmap shows a lot of 0.5GPU slots stranded. Attach/backfill latency spiking, applications reporting degraded throughput.

jess: can you paste node logs? iirc we saw conntrack/table-full errors during the last warm-pool rollout.

marco: here's a representative snippet from k8s-nv-12 around 04:33:

```
Apr 12 04:33:21 k8s-nv-12 kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
Apr 12 04:33:22 kubelet[2345]: attach: timeout waiting for device attach: context deadline exceeded
Apr 12 04:33:22 kubelet[2345]: evicting pod small-trainer-abc (small-pod) due to attach timeout
```

sunita: warm-pool attach p95 jumped from ~12s to ~55s between 04:25-04:40. API errors include "rpc error: code = Unknown desc = websocket: close 1006" and intermittent TLS handshakes. looks like conntrack + conn reuse problem.

infra-bot: [alert] ap-southeast2: small-pod-evict-rate > 100/min for 15m (alert_id: infra:small-evict:3543).

lee: confirmed on the nodes: nf_conntrack_count==65536, table_size default. We can bump net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max but that increases kernel memory per node. Alternative: reduce parallel attach concurrency from warm-pool controller.

ops-lead: immediate mitigation options (short-term):
- relax small-pod anti-affinity to allow tighter binpacking across same-rack nodes (reduces cross-rack attaches)
- throttle warm-pool attach parallelism (controller config)
- canary bump conntrack on 10 warm nodes and monitor

jess: +1 to throttling parallelism and a scheduler tweak. Also propose scheduler soft-preference to coalesce tiny pods onto fewer nodes (coalesce N=4) so we reduce number of attach operations. cheaper than adding capacity.

marco: coalesce preference sounds good. i'll draft a tiny-scheduler change: prefer node with existing tiny-pods, weight=+100, limit to nodes with free GPU >= 0.5. will send PR for canary cluster.

sunita: i will own the rollout. plan: 1) bump conntrack on 10 warm nodes in ap-southeast2-a at 10:45 UTC (sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000) 2) deploy scheduler coalesce policy to canary at 10:50 3) throttle warm-pool attach parallelism by 30% 4) observe 30m. dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/infra/frag/ap-southeast2 (watch pending-small-pods, evict-rate, attach-p95)

ops-lead: please document rollback clearly. SLA for the canary: evictions < 10/min and attach-p95 < 20s within 30m or rollback. Also tag the canary nodes with `canary=conntrack` for easy revert.

lee: small caution: increasing conntrack can push node memory up under high-conn churn. if we see oom-killer or slab growth, revert immediately and rely on attach-throttle.

jess: cost note — if coalesce reduces node spread we may increase CPU pressure on a few nodes; monitor CPU and GPU util. But overall avoids spinning up new instances which would have a higher bill.

marco: i'll update the incident doc with the plan and add links to the PR and rollback steps.

sunita: pushing canary now — bumping conntrack on 10 nodes, enabling scheduler coalesce on canary cluster. will post updates in 10m. :rocket:

lee: thanks — i'll watch node memory and conntrack slab stats. if anything weird, i'll revert net.sysctl and lower warm-pool concurrency.

ops-lead: once canary is stable, we need a follow-up to: 1) make coalesce policy opt-in per-tenant, 2) add telemetry to count attach ops avoided by coalescing, 3) consider longer-term: warm-pool attach backoff/resume strategy.

sunita: noted. canary live at 10:50 UTC, initial metrics look promising (evictions down ~40% in first 6m). continuing to monitor. :eyes:
